model_confidence: How much the model trusts this reading, based on coverage and consistency of the source data. It is not a hit-rate probability.
class_composition_score: How this name compares with the others in the same asset class in the motor snapshot.

fred_10y_spread.meaning: Difference between the 10-year and 2-year Treasury yields — the slope of the yield curve.
fred_10y_spread.read: Positive (steep) is a normal cycle. Near zero is flat. Negative (inverted) historically raises recession risk and often favors cash or shorter duration.

security_score: Quantitative score of the individual name (security layer), combining ticker-specific indicators in the motor model.
global_motor_models: The name's score compared with the average or benchmark of its asset class in the motor.
entry_validated: Whether price, volume, and momentum confirm a technical entry point, independent of the motor's recommendation.
entry_not_validated: Technical conditions have not confirmed an entry yet — wait for confirmation even with a favorable motor signal.
strong_reduce: The motor recommends reducing the position with high conviction; it does not imply an automatic full sale.

stochastic_rsi.meaning: Stochastic applied to RSI — a second oscillator that shows how stretched RSI itself is.
stochastic_rsi.read: Above 80: overbought; below 20: oversold. A turn back from those zones is the usable signal, not the extreme alone.

cci.meaning: Commodity Channel Index: how far price sits from its typical average, in units of mean deviation.
cci.read: Above +100 the name is extended higher; below −100, lower. The motor treats a turn back through those bands as the signal.

macd_level.meaning: MACD line: 12-day EMA minus 26-day EMA. It measures whether short-term momentum is faster than the medium trend.
macd_level.read: Above zero favors upside; below zero favors downside. A cross of the signal line (9-day EMA of MACD) confirms a turn.

stochastic_fast.meaning: Fast stochastic %K: where the close sits inside the recent high–low range (0–100).
stochastic_fast.read: Above 80: overbought; below 20: oversold. Buy when %K crosses back up through %D in the oversold zone; sell on the opposite cross up high.

williams_r.meaning: Williams %R: an inverted stochastic on a −100 to 0 scale.
williams_r.read: Near 0 is overbought; near −100 is oversold. A move back from the extreme is the reading that matters.

bull_bear_power.meaning: Elder’s Bull/Bear Power: high and low versus an exponential average — buying vs selling pressure.
bull_bear_power.read: Positive net power favors bulls; negative favors bears. Rising bull power with price is confirmation; fading power warns the move is tired.

bollinger_bands: Volatility band around price. Compression indicates low volatility (possible breakout); expansion, high volatility.

moving_averages.meaning: A moving average is the typical price over N sessions. SMA weights every day equally; EMA reacts faster to the latest prints.
moving_averages.read: Price above the average = strength for that horizon. Price below = weakness. A 50-day cross above the 200-day is a golden cross; the reverse is a death cross.

oscillators.meaning: Short-term momentum tools (RSI, stochastic, MACD, and similar). They ask whether the name is stretched, not whether the class is cheap.
oscillators.read: Buy/Sell here means a reversal from an extreme, not a forecast. Many Neutrals in a strong trend is normal — oscillators stay pinned.

motor_signal: Quantitative reading from the decision motor by class and name, combining macro, regime, and sleeve indicators.
macro_risk: Macro and systemic-risk block (yield curve, spreads, volatility) that contextualizes the name's score.
convergence: Comparison between the motor signal (quantitative) and the technical signal (price/momentum) to avoid unexplained contradictory readings.
technical_rating: Visual summary of the motor score. The scale changes by class: 0–1 percentile vs peers in two-layer models, or −1 to +1 directional otherwise.
allocation_stance: How much of the asset class to hold in aggregate, according to the regime model (macro, carry, curve). It does not say whether this specific name is a buy.
instrument_quality: How this name compares with peers in the same class on the same day. It is a relative ranking, not a price direction.
entry_timing: Whether price confirms an entry now. Independent of the allocation recommendation: the class can be favored without this being a good moment to buy.
forecast_range: Likely price range projected from recent volatility, not a point forecast. Historical coverage shows how often the range was right in the past.
forecast_coverage: Share of times realized price stayed inside the projected range in walk-forward tests. Near the nominal level (68% or 95%) indicates a well-calibrated range.
fibonacci: Retracement and extension levels calculated on a confirmed swing. They are reference zones, not guaranteed targets.
support_resistance: Prices where the name reversed in the recent past, detected by swing pivots confirmed on both sides.

rsi.meaning: Relative Strength Index: average gains versus average losses over 14 sessions, on a 0–100 scale.
rsi.read: Above 70 the name is stretched higher; below 30, lower. The table signals Buy only when RSI leaves oversold heading up, and Sell when it leaves overbought heading down.

adx.meaning: Average Directional Index: strength of the trend, not its direction. +DI and −DI say who is in control.
adx.read: ADX above 20 = a defined trend. If +DI is above −DI, the trend is up; the reverse is down. Low ADX means a range — ignore trend-following signals.

awesome_oscillator.meaning: Difference between 5- and 34-period averages of the bar’s midpoint. It compares very short momentum with a slower pulse.
awesome_oscillator.read: Crossing from below zero to above is a momentum turn up; the opposite is a turn down. Color/histogram rising while still negative is only early, not a buy on its own.

momentum.meaning: Raw difference between today’s close and the close 10 sessions ago.
momentum.read: The level is less important than the direction: rising momentum supports the move; falling momentum says the move is slowing even if price is still up.

ultimate_oscillator.meaning: Weighted blend of 7-, 14-, and 28-session buying pressure, built to reduce the false turns of a single window.
ultimate_oscillator.read: Above 70 is extended higher; below 30, lower. A failure to make a new oscillator high with price is a divergence — treat as a warning, not an automatic sale.

ichimoku.meaning: Ichimoku: conversion line, base line, and a cloud projected forward. It is a full trend system, not a single oscillator.
ichimoku.read: Bullish when price is above the cloud, conversion above base, and the cloud is rising. Mixed readings (price in the cloud) mean wait.

vwma.meaning: Volume-weighted moving average: days with more trading pull the average toward that price.
vwma.read: Price above VWMA means the heavy volume was done at lower prices (buyers in control). Below means the volume sat higher (sellers in control).

hull_ma.meaning: Hull moving average: a faster average that cuts the usual lag of SMA/EMA, at the cost of more noise.
hull_ma.read: Price crossing above is a quicker strength signal; crossing below is quicker weakness. Use it with a slower average so one whip does not decide the trade.

pivot_points: Levels calculated from the previous period's high, low, and close. P is equilibrium, R1–R3 are resistances and S1–S3 supports. Because they stay fixed until the period closes, they work as targets set in advance.

motor_col_value.meaning: The raw reading of this indicator on the snapshot date — a yield, a spread, a percent, or a z-score, depending on the row.
motor_col_value.read: This is the unscaled print. The Rank and Stance columns are what enter the Security Score; a raw 0.000 vol is not a 0.00 rank.

motor_col_percentile.meaning: Directed 0-to-1 peer rank of this ingredient on the snapshot date. 0.5 is the median name in the class that day.
motor_col_percentile.read: This is the number that is multiplied by the recipe weight. Inverted pillars (vol, expense, leverage) are already flipped, so higher is always better for the score.

motor_col_stance.meaning: Glanceable band of the peer rank: Adds (≥ 0.65), Neutral (around the median), or Drags (< 0.35).
motor_col_stance.read: Adds means this ingredient is lifting the score. Drags means this is the weak spot. Neutral is the class median.

motor_col_action.meaning: How this row is leaning inside the motor right now: Buy, Neutral, or Sell.
motor_col_action.read: It comes from the sign of the contribution, not from a broker rating. Several Neutrals plus one strong driver is normal. On two-layer Security Scores prefer Rank and Stance — contribution is always positive.

motor_col_contribution.meaning: This row’s weighted input to the Security Score or class score (weight × directed percentile or z).
motor_col_contribution.read: Larger absolute contribution = this indicator is doing more of the work. The sign says whether it is helping or hurting the score.

motor_col_zscore.meaning: How unusual today’s value is versus this indicator’s own recent history (typically ~1 year).
motor_col_zscore.read: Near 0 = typical. Around ±1 = a bit unusual. Beyond ±2 = a rare print. Direction (positive vs negative) follows the indicator’s own scale.

volume_vs_media.meaning: Traded volume versus its recent average — unusual activity, not how liquid the name is in absolute terms.
volume_vs_media.read: A spike versus its own average can mean unusual flow. It is not the Cash Security Score liquidity pillar.

volume_negociado.meaning: Raw traded volume on the snapshot day. Liquidity pillar of the Security Score in Cash (50%), Treasuries (20%), IG (15%), HY (15%), and TIPS (15%).
volume_negociado.read: Higher percentile vs peers = more volume that day = easier to enter and exit. The motor does not invert this percentile. US Stocks use dollar volume instead.

volume_dolar.meaning: Dollar volume on the snapshot day: last close × shares traded. Liquidity pillar of the US Stocks (20%), Emerging Markets (20%), REITs (20%), Precious Metals (25%), Energy (20%), and MLP (20%) Security Scores.
volume_dolar.read: Higher percentile vs peers = more dollars changed hands = easier to enter and exit. Share count would favor cheap names; this does not. The motor does not invert this percentile.

vol_realizada.meaning: Realized volatility over the last 20 sessions (standard deviation of daily returns).
vol_realizada.read: For Cash, High Yield, Preferred, US Stocks, International Stocks, REITs, and MLP, lower is better: the motor inverts the percentile so a calmer name ranks higher vs peers that day. A market-wide vol spike does not single out one name. On preferreds and MLPs, extra swing is a credit-stress symptom on income paper.

preco_vs_mm50.meaning: How far the last price sits from its 50-day moving average, as a percent.
preco_vs_mm50.read: Near the average is normal. A large gap is an extension. In most risk assets, above the average is strength; in Cash the motor treats a large gap as an anomaly, not as a bullish trend.

preco_vs_mm50_z_abs.meaning: Absolute z-score of price versus its 50-day average: (price − MA50) / 50-day price standard deviation.
preco_vs_mm50_z_abs.read: Small |z| = the name is drifting in line with its own usual pace (healthy for cash ETFs). Large |z| = a real dislocation. The motor ranks the smaller |z| as safer.

preco_vs_mm200.meaning: How far the last price sits from its 200-day moving average — the long trend line.
preco_vs_mm200.read: Above the 200-day is a longer-term uptrend; below is a downtrend. A cross of this line is slower and more meaningful than a 50-day wiggle.

trend.meaning: Combined reading of the 50- and 200-day averages: whether the name is in a confirmed uptrend versus peers.
trend.read: Higher percentile = stronger trend versus the rest of the class on the same day. It is a ranking, not a promise that the trend continues.

dividend_yield.meaning: Income the name is currently distributing, as a percent of price. In Preferred, REITs, and MLP the Security Score haircuts a yield that spiked versus its own 1-year history (yield trap).
dividend_yield.read: A stable high coupon still ranks high. A yield that jumped only because price collapsed is shrunk before ranking, so distress is not paid as extra carry.

duration_efetiva.meaning: Effective duration: how much the bond-like name’s price tends to move when yields move 1%. In IG this is a duration-band fit vs term premium; in TIPS, vs today’s 10-year real yield (DFII10) — not “higher is better”.
duration_efetiva.read: Names in the same maturity bucket get the same fit that day — it is not a paper-specific signal. High term premium / real yield favors the long bucket; low favors the short bucket.

cot_net_position.meaning: Weekly CFTC Commitments of Traders: net speculative positioning in Treasury futures (crowding).
cot_net_position.read: Held at the last weekly print until the next CFTC release — no interpolation. In the Treasuries score this is inverted: higher crowding lowers the class-level contribution. It does not rank one ETF against another.

crowding.meaning: Class-level positioning: for precious metals, CFTC gold COT (`cot_gold_net`), falling back to GLD tonnes if COT is missing.
crowding.read: Lives in PreciousRegimeScore, not in the Security Score. On a given day every metal ETF sees the same print, so it cannot pick GLD over IAU. High crowding is a class-level caution, same idea as Treasuries COT.

preco_vs_mm50_dur.meaning: Price vs its 50-day average, divided by the ETF’s modified duration so a long bond is not scored as stronger momentum just because it moves more for the same yield change.
preco_vs_mm50_dur.read: Compared across Treasuries, IG, or TIPS on the same day. Higher percentile = stronger duration-adjusted uptrend (rate-risk-adjusted, not raw price gap). For TIPS this uses the ETF share price, not a TIPS dirty bond price.

rsi_14_dur.meaning: 14-day RSI computed on daily percent change divided by modified duration — momentum in yield space, not raw price RSI.
rsi_14_dur.read: Higher percentile = stronger duration-adjusted momentum. Unlike Cash, Treasuries, IG, and TIPS keep RSI because those sleeves have genuine rate-reversal cycles.

preco_vs_mm50_oil.meaning: Price vs its 50-day average, divided by max(|beta vs USO|, 0.25) so a high-beta E&P is not scored as stronger trend just because oil moved.
preco_vs_mm50_oil.read: Compared across Energy names on the same day. Higher percentile = stronger oil-beta-adjusted uptrend. Natural-gas names with tiny oil beta are floored at 0.25 so the ratio does not explode.

rsi_14_oil.meaning: 14-day RSI computed on daily percent change divided by max(|beta vs USO|, 0.25) — momentum per unit of oil sensitivity.
rsi_14_oil.read: RSI is scale-invariant on a single name; the oil-beta bias is fixed mostly on the trend pillar. Kept for consistency with duration-adjusted RSI in Treasuries/IG/TIPS.

nav_discount.meaning: Price versus last reported NAV per share. A discount means the market price is below the portfolio’s book. In BDCs the NAV level is quarterly (hold-last); the ratio uses the as-of close.
nav_discount.read: A wider discount ranks higher (inverted premium). Cheap NAV with low non-accrual is a value candidate; cheap NAV with rising non-accrual is a likely trap — the market may not trust the reported book.

non_accrual.meaning: Share of the BDC loan book that has stopped accruing interest (borrowers in distress). Parsed from the 10-Q/10-K; hold-last until the next filing.
non_accrual.read: Lower is better. This is the credit-quality check on a cheap NAV. The print is lagged: a loan enters non-accrual after the problem is already visible.

nii_coverage.meaning: Net investment income divided by dividends paid. Whether the BDC’s operating income covers the distribution. Hold-last from the 10-Q; reported NII, not fee-adjusted.
nii_coverage.read: Higher coverage ranks higher. This replaces raw dividend yield so a distressed name whose yield jumped because the price collapsed does not win. Incentive fees are not stripped out of NII.

fcf_coverage.meaning: Free cash flow divided by dividends paid (operating cash flow minus capex). Hold-last from SEC companyfacts for infrastructure issuers.
fcf_coverage.read: Higher coverage ranks higher. This is the trap check next to yield-vs-own-history: a utility whose price fell still needs FCF to pay the coupon. ETFs have no 10-Q and sit at the median.

ev_ebitda.meaning: Enterprise value / EBITDA versus the name’s own last 12 quarters (z-score). Inverted so a discount to the name’s typical multiple ranks higher.
ev_ebitda.read: Cheaper than this issuer’s own history is better — not cheaper than a tower vs a utility. That is how the sleeve avoids mixing subsectors into one valuation rank.

debt_ebitda.meaning: Total debt / EBITDA. Hold-last from SEC companyfacts. Inverted: lower leverage ranks higher versus other infrastructure names that day.
debt_ebitda.read: Infrastructure can carry more debt than the broad market, but inside the sleeve the less leveraged name still ranks better. ETFs sit at the median.

expense_ratio.meaning: Annual fund fee. In Precious Metals and FX this is an inverted Security Score pillar (cheaper ranks higher).
expense_ratio.read: Lower expense = more of the exposure’s return stays with you. The motor inverts the percentile so 0.5 is still the median-cost name that day. In FX the prospectus fee is the declared cost; tracking error is the realized cost.

custo_efetivo_inv.meaning: Inverted expense / holding cost for FX vehicles — cheaper access ranks higher.
custo_efetivo_inv.read: Higher score = you pay less to hold the currency exposure. It is not a view on whether the dollar will rise.

adequacao_fiscal.meaning: Distance of |beta vs UUP| to the FX class target (25th percentile of the sleeve that day). Fit = 1 − |P(|β|) − 0.25|.
adequacao_fiscal.read: Closer to the target is better in both directions — not more dollar beta. Two funds with the same |beta| get the same fit: this is a vehicle bucket, not a call on the dollar. Direction lives in ConversionPaceScore.

dollar_fit.meaning: Distance of |beta vs UUP| to the FX class target (25th percentile of the sleeve that day). Fit = 1 − |P(|β|) − 0.25|.
dollar_fit.read: Closer to the target is better in both directions — not more dollar beta. Two funds with the same |beta| get the same fit: this is a vehicle bucket, not a call on the dollar. Direction lives in ConversionPaceScore.

fx_carry.meaning: Policy-rate differential of the currency the ETF holds versus Fed funds. Long-dollar funds use Fed minus the EUR/JPY basket. Hold-last. Monotonic: higher carry ranks higher.
fx_carry.read: You are paid (on average) to hold a higher-yielding currency. This is the ticker’s carry — not the class Fed−ECB number in ConversionPaceScore, which is the same for every name that day. Carry can reverse sharply in risk-off; there is no vol offset in this version.

tracking_error.meaning: Annualized 63-day standard deviation of ETF daily return minus the FRED spot pair (DEXUSEU, inverted DEXJPUS, or DTWEXBGS). Inverted: lower tracking error ranks higher.
tracking_error.read: This is realized cost — roll and leakage the prospectus fee misses. CEW has no single spot pair and sits at the median.

hedge_fit.meaning: Distance of |beta vs UUP| to the International Stocks class target (35th percentile of the sleeve that day). Fit = 1 − |P(|β|) − 0.35|.
hedge_fit.read: Closer to the target is better in both directions — not more dollar beta, not less. Two ETFs with the same |beta| get the same fit: this is a regional/FX bucket, not an issuer signal. USD-weak/strong stays in IntlEquityRegimeScore.

beta_fit.meaning: Distance of signed beta vs USO to the Energy class target (70th percentile of the sleeve that day). Fit = 1 − |P(β) − 0.70|. USO is the WTI proxy.
beta_fit.read: Closer to the target is better in both directions — not more oil beta. Two ETFs with the same USO beta get the same fit: this is a subsector bucket (E&P vs integrated vs gas), not an issuer signal. Inventories, rigs, and WTI COT stay in EnergyRegimeScore.

china_fit.meaning: Distance of beta vs FXI to the Emerging Markets class target (60th percentile of the sleeve that day). Fit = 1 − |P(β) − 0.60|. Beta is signed, not absolute.
china_fit.read: Closer to the target is better in both directions — not more China beta. Two ETFs with the same FXI beta get the same fit: this is a China-mix bucket (EEM vs EMXC), not an issuer signal. China-as-a-bloc stays in EMEquityRegimeScore.

catalyst_density.meaning: Proxy for nearby FDA / pipeline catalysts in biotech (calendar density).
catalyst_density.read: Higher density = more event risk and more optionality in the next window. It is not a probability that the trial succeeds.

yield_real_caixa.meaning: Real cash yield: 3-month T-bill (DTB3) minus inflation (CPI). What cash pays after prices rise.
yield_real_caixa.read: Above zero: cash preserves purchasing power. Near or below zero: sitting in bills loses real value — the regime model then leans away from overweight cash.

spread_10y_2y.meaning: 10-year minus 2-year Treasury yield. Same curve as the FRED 10y–2y spread.
spread_10y_2y.read: Steep (positive) supports risk and longer duration. Flat or inverted favors cash, floating rate, and caution on cyclicals.

fed_cut_probability.meaning: Market-implied chance of Fed cuts over the next ~6 months (CME FedWatch).
fed_cut_probability.read: Rising cut odds usually help duration and risk assets, and reduce the need to hoard cash. Falling cut odds (or hike pricing) do the opposite. For cash, high cut probability is a reason to look beyond T-bills.

term_premium.meaning: Extra yield investors demand to hold a long Treasury instead of rolling shorts (ACM / FRED THREEFYTP10).
term_premium.read: Rising term premium = bonds are cheaper / yields compensating more for duration. Falling term premium = long bonds are rich. The Treasury regime uses this as the main valuation pillar.

bond_vol_proxy.meaning: Proxy for bond-market volatility (TLT implied or realized vol) — not the official MOVE index.
bond_vol_proxy.read: High bond vol = unstable rates; the model reduces duration risk. Low vol = a calmer backdrop for adding Treasuries.

yield_real_10y.meaning: 10-year real yield: nominal 10-year minus inflation breakeven (DGS10 − T10YIE), or TIPS yield DFII10.
yield_real_10y.read: Rising real yields tighten financial conditions and usually hurt gold, long duration, and rich growth. Falling real yields do the reverse. High real yield can be a better entry for TIPS/Treasuries.

yield_10y.meaning: Nominal 10-year Treasury yield (DGS10). The risk-free long rate everything else is priced against.
yield_10y.read: Rising 10-year yield pressures REITs, preferreds, and long bonds. Falling yield is usually a tailwind for those sleeves. Read it with inflation: a rise from growth is different from a rise from inflation fear.

fed_funds.meaning: Federal funds rate — the overnight policy rate set by the Fed.
fed_funds.read: A high or rising funds rate tightens liquidity and often weighs on equities and credit. Cuts ease conditions. The level matters less than the direction the market has not yet priced.

vix.meaning: CBOE VIX: implied 30-day volatility on the S&P 500. A fear gauge, not a forecast of the next print.
vix.read: Low VIX (teens) = complacent / cheap hedges. Spikes (20s–30s+) = stress; the motor treats very high VIX as a risk-off input, sometimes a better entry for equities after the spike.

dxy.meaning: US Dollar Index — the dollar versus a basket of major currencies.
dxy.read: A strong dollar typically hurts gold, EM, and international equities in USD terms. A weakening dollar is a tailwind for those sleeves and for commodities.

cpi.meaning: US CPI — the official consumer inflation print.
cpi.read: Rising CPI that the market has not priced is hostile to long bonds and gold’s real-rate story. Cooling CPI supports duration and can support risk. Always read next to breakevens: surprise vs what is already in the price.

dfii10.meaning: 10-year TIPS real yield (FRED DFII10). The market’s real risk-free rate.
dfii10.read: Same reading as real yield: up is tighter conditions (headwind for gold and long duration); down is easier. For precious metals this is often the single most important macro input.

wti.meaning: West Texas Intermediate crude oil price.
wti.read: Rising WTI supports energy commodities and MLPs; falling WTI does the opposite. A spike can also be a growth/inflation shock for the rest of the book — not automatically “good.”

henry_hub.meaning: Henry Hub natural-gas price, the US gas benchmark.
henry_hub.read: Higher gas supports midstream / energy infrastructure that is volume- or price-sensitive to gas. A collapse in gas can cut MLP distributions even if oil is fine.

eurusd.read: A rising EURUSD is a weaker dollar. That usually helps international assets in USD and can weigh on pure-dollar cash. The FX sleeve uses it as the core rate pair.

ig_oas.meaning: Investment-grade option-adjusted spread — extra yield of IG corporates over Treasuries.
ig_oas.read: Wider OAS = credit is cheaper / more stressed (better entry if you want IG). Tight OAS = little compensation for default risk. A sudden widening is a risk-off signal. This is a class index (ICE BofA via FRED), so it feeds IGRegimeScore — it cannot rank one IG ETF against another.

delta_ig_spread_20d.meaning: 20-day change in the IG credit spread.
delta_ig_spread_20d.read: Spreads widening over two weeks = credit deteriorating now. Tightening = healing. The motor uses the short window to catch a break that the slow OAS level would miss.

ig_bbb_aaa_spread.meaning: Gap between BBB and AAA IG spreads — quality inside investment grade.
ig_bbb_aaa_spread.read: A fatter BBB–AAA gap means investors are demanding more to own the weakest IG names. That is early credit stress, even if headline IG OAS still looks fine.

hy_oas.meaning: High-yield option-adjusted spread — extra yield of junk bonds over Treasuries.
hy_oas.read: Wide HY OAS = the market is paying you more to take credit risk (or is scared). Tight HY OAS = little cushion if defaults rise. This is a class index (ICE BofA via FRED), including BB/B/CCC slices — it feeds HYRegimeScore. The current scored sleeve is all broad HY, so it cannot rank one ETF against another.

delta_hy_spread_20d.read: Fast widening = credit event in progress. Fast tightening after a spike can be a bounce, not a new cycle. Pair it with the level of HY OAS.

hy_quality_ratio.meaning: Quality mix inside high yield (better-rated HY versus weaker names).
hy_quality_ratio.read: Deteriorating quality (more weight on weaker credits) is a warning even if the headline spread has not blown out. Improving quality supports holding HY.

hy_distress_proxy_score.meaning: Proxy for HY distress: percentile of CCC spreads plus HY ETF realized vol. It is not the official S&P distress ratio.
hy_distress_proxy_score.read: High score = the weakest credits and HY volatility are already stressed. Treat as a reduce / wait signal for HY and BDCs, not as a precise default forecast.

hy_minus_ig.meaning: High-yield spread minus investment-grade spread — the extra junk premium.
hy_minus_ig.read: A compressed HY−IG gap means you are barely paid to step down in quality. A wide gap can justify HY over IG if you want the risk.

hy_bb_spread.meaning: Option-adjusted spread of BB-rated high yield (the highest-quality junk).
hy_bb_spread.read: BB is the “crossover” bucket. Widening here is a broader credit problem, not just CCC distress. Tight BB with wide CCC is a barbell inside HY.

hy_b_spread.meaning: Option-adjusted spread of B-rated high yield.
hy_b_spread.read: B sits between BB and CCC. Persistent widening here is the middle of the credit stack leaking — usually a reason to cut HY beta.

sloos.meaning: Fed Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey — how many banks are tightening lending standards.
sloos.read: More officers tightening = credit will get scarcer with a lag (bad for HY, BDCs, preferreds). Easing standards support those sleeves. The print is quarterly — do not treat it as a daily ticker.

preferred_spread.meaning: Extra yield of preferreds (e.g. PFF) over the 10-year Treasury.
preferred_spread.read: A wider preferred spread = more income versus duration, or more fear about banks/issuers. Tight spread = you are not paid much to own preferreds instead of Treasuries.

delta_preferred_spread_20d.read: A fast widening is a bank / credit scare. Tightening is healing. Use it as a short-term stress flag on top of the level.

kre_vs_spy_60d.meaning: 60-day relative performance of regional banks (KRE) versus the S&P 500.
kre_vs_spy_60d.read: KRE lagging SPY is a bank-stress warning for preferreds. KRE leading is a healthier backdrop for bank-issued preferreds.

breakeven_5y5y.meaning: 5y5y inflation breakeven (FRED T5YIFR) — what the market prices for inflation five years from now, for five years.
breakeven_5y5y.read: Rising 5y5y = inflation expectations un-anchoring (supports TIPS, can hurt nominal long bonds). Falling 5y5y = disinflation priced in. Compare with realized CPI.

cpi_breakeven_gap.meaning: Gap between realized CPI and the inflation the TIPS market is pricing.
cpi_breakeven_gap.read: CPI running above breakevens means TIPS may still be cheap vs incoming inflation. The opposite means the market already paid up for inflation that is cooling.

tips_liquidity_proxy.meaning: Proxy for how easily TIPS are trading (not a full bid-ask tape).
tips_liquidity_proxy.read: Stressed liquidity = wider gaps and jumpy NAV — size down. Normal liquidity means the TIPS sleeve can be used as a real-yield tool again.

pe_rel_intl_us.meaning: International equity P/E relative to US P/E (cheap or expensive versus SPX).
pe_rel_intl_us.read: A low relative P/E means international is cheaper than the US on earnings. That is a valuation tailwind, not a timing signal — pair it with the dollar and VIX.

pe_rel_em_us.meaning: Emerging-market P/E relative to US P/E.
pe_rel_em_us.read: EM cheaper than the US (low ratio) is the valuation case for the sleeve. EM richer than the US needs a growth or flow story. Always read with the dollar.

gdp_growth_em.meaning: Emerging-market GDP growth (World Bank / lagged official data).
gdp_growth_em.read: Faster EM growth versus developed markets supports the EM sleeve. Because the print is slow, treat it as a regime backdrop, not a weekly trigger.

distribution_yield_spread.meaning: MLP / midstream distribution yield minus the 10-year Treasury — extra income versus duration.
distribution_yield_spread.read: A wide spread means you are paid more to own the pipeline sleeve instead of Treasuries. A tight spread means the yield is not compensating for equity/energy risk.
